title: Spend the power-variation root budget on outside-domain roots: 391 → 2987 certified (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof with an exact checker. No new κ, supplier or construction claim.**

PR #5788's general-rank power-variation certificate (`scripts/compare_power_variation.py`, `docs/research/recursive-power-variation.md`) bounds all real roots of `F(t)=Σ c_r r^t` by the number `V` of coefficient sign changes. It spends that budget only at `t=0`, `t=1` and inside `(0,1)`. When roots lie at `t<0` or `t>1`, the budget stays unspent and the report is `inconclusive`. That document's Open next question asks for a proof of such an outside-domain root.

This package certifies those roots exactly and subtracts them before the interior count:

- the sign of `F` as `t→−∞` is the sign of the smallest-rank coefficient, and as `t→+∞` the sign of the largest;
- `F(k)` is an exact rational at each integer `k`;
- each exact zero at a listed integer and each strict sign change between adjacent points on `(−∞,0)` or `(1,∞)` is a distinct root outside `[0,1]`.

PR #5788's closure rule then runs on the reduced budget `V − e_0 − e_1 − W`. The proof is in the package README.

Example: `4 − 8·2^t − 3^t + 2·6^t = 2(2^t − 1/2)(3^t − 4)` has `V=2` and equal endpoint values `−3`, and #5788 reports `inconclusive`. An exact zero at `t=−1` and a sign change on `(1,2)` use the whole budget, so the extended check proves the difference is uniformly lower on `0<t<1`.

## Evidence

`research/power-variation-outside-roots/verify.py`, about 13 s:

- two fixtures move from `inconclusive` under #5788 to `uniformly_lower`, with the stated witnesses;
- **factored oracle census**: every product of one to three factors `q·a^t − p` with `a ∈ {2,3,5}` and 15 thresholds `p/q`, 4,455 invoices in total. Roots are known in closed form. Interior membership, integer roots and the sign at `t=1/2` are exact integer tests. Results:
  - #5788 certifies **391**;
  - this extension certifies **2,987**, of which **2,596** are newly settled;
  - **0** false certificates, 0 budget overruns and 0 changed #5788 verdicts.
- **failure controls**: two mutations are rejected by the same oracle.
  - Swapped asymptotic signs: 887 false certificates, 2,026 budget overruns and 94 changed verdicts.
  - Double-counting zero endpoints: 463 false certificates, 491 overruns and 104 changed verdicts.

The verifier fails closed without `assert`, so it also checks under `-O`. The shared script is imported unchanged and pinned as a live input.

Reproduce from the repository root. The local runs used CPython 3.12.14 at `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`.

```sh
python3.12 -B research/power-variation-outside-roots/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/power-variation-outside-roots/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/power-variation-outside-roots
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/power-variation-outside-roots --check-source-history
```

All four passed locally. The registered check reported `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`, and the commit check reported `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

- This change covers invoice arithmetic only. It certifies no construction, source extraction, native operator, compiler endpoint, supplier admission or κ, and the selected result is unchanged.
- The census is a finite exact check of the implementation. It does not prove completeness.
- Two outside roots in the same unit interval are not witnessed. The report then stays `inconclusive`, which is sound.
- Touching (even-multiplicity) interior roots remain unresolved, as in #5788.
- `scripts/compare_power_variation.py` is not modified; folding the rule into it is a maintainer decision.
- No source invoice from the selected ledger was run.
- Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Finer outside brackets: extend directed enclosures to `r^(k+s)` so that two roots in one outside unit interval can be separated. Test case: `(2^t − 5/2)(3^t − 4)`, with both roots in `(1,2)`.
- Run the extension on the pinned P104 ledger exported by the selected-invoice tool (#5735) and on its declared edits. Does any committed invoice that #5788 leaves inconclusive become certified?
- Find an exact certificate for touching interior roots in general-rank exponential sums.

## Related open work

No open PR studies the power-variation root budget or the #5788 comparator. Searches covered the title and body terms "power variation", "outside-domain", "root budget" and "Descartes". Rechecked after CI: #5977 (plane-port clique savings) and #5978 (address-twist syzygies), opened since this claim, study different objects and compute no shared quantity.

## CI notes

All checks passed on head `cf1504a968ab242c99c0907a722593b490ce8a39`: `plan` and `replay (research/power-variation-outside-roots)`, run https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40564990746.

## Credit

The root budget, endpoint multiplicities, interior brackets, invoice schema and directed power engine come from Ali Romman's #5788 and #5746 and their credited predecessors: zxv's signed-invoice interface, woklerx's T16 unique-crossing proof and mightyOil's moment-order audit. The generalized Descartes rule is classical. The outside-domain witness rule, its proof, the oracle census and the controls are new and were produced by Nick Petalas.
